name: VARoleArbiterBlogCelebrityClaim

custom.system_prompt: Devon sends Marisol a claim from an unfamiliar blog about a celebrity or product, excited about it. Marisol, a copywriter, immediately clocks the writing style as suspicious. They ask Sigma to help assess whether the blog is a credible source.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Casual apartment hangout, background music low, phone sounds

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Devon shares an exciting claim about a celebrity or product from an unfamiliar blog, fully bought in. Marisol, a marketing copywriter, immediately recognizes the writing style as designed to be shared rather than to inform, and is skeptical the site itself is a real, reliable outlet. They ask Sigma to help assess whether the blog is a credible source. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Devon
user1.tts_prompt: Excited, ready to share it further

user2.name: Marisol
user2.tts_prompt: Sardonic, quick to spot the technique

variations.context: Friends disagreeing about the credibility of an unfamiliar blog making a celebrity or product claim

setting.mood: Devon's excitement meeting Marisol's professional skepticism about persuasive writing
setting.relationship_dynamic: Marisol enjoys her role as the group's reality-check friend, sometimes past the point of being fully fair about it
setting.background: Devon is already drafting a message to share the claim further before checking anything
setting.conversation_style: Short, casual, Marisol quick and a little sardonic

scenario_template.topic: Devon shares the claim, excited to pass it along; Marisol immediately flags the blog's writing style as manipulative-sounding rather than addressing whether the claim is actually true or false yet. A few short exchanges.
scenario_template.note: Marisol's first instinct is about technique, not truth.

scenario_template.topic: Marisol asks Sigma to check whether the blog itself is a credible, known outlet, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, is this actually a real outlet, or is this just an SEO content site?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma assesses the blog's apparent standing — whether it has an editorial track record, whether the claim is picked up anywhere more established — and gives an honest, specific read rather than confirming Marisol's dismissiveness wholesale if the picture is more mixed. One or two short sentences.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be fair — even a lesser-known outlet isn't automatically false, just less corroborated.

scenario_template.topic: Devon is a little embarrassed but points out he's allowed to enjoy a story before fact-checking it; Marisol is satisfied but is gently called out for being reflexively dismissive rather than actually checking first herself. Keep this realistic — Marisol's certainty gets lightly complicated too.
scenario_template.mood: Mixed — both get a small correction
scenario_template.note: This shouldn't be a clean win for Marisol either — her instinct was right but her process wasn't rigorous.

scenario_template.topic: They agree Devon will hold off sharing it until it's corroborated, one short line each.

user1.name: Devon
user1.role: Enthusiastic aspiring filmmaker, drawn to a good story before checking whether it's true. Speaks in short sentences. A little embarrassed at being flagged but pushes back that enjoying a story isn't the same as being gullible.

user2.name: Marisol
user2.role: Sharp, sardonic marketing copywriter, quick to spot persuasive writing technique. Speaks in short sentences. Gets gently called out for being reflexively dismissive rather than actually checking first — her certainty isn't fully vindicated either.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Assesses an unfamiliar outlet's credibility fairly — noting real red flags but not dismissing lesser-known sources automatically as false, only as less corroborated. Evaluates the source, not either friend's general judgment.

conversation_structure: This is a source-credibility case about an unfamiliar outlet — Sigma must distinguish 'unfamiliar/uncorroborated' from 'definitely false'
Sigma gives a fair, specific read rather than simply validating the more skeptical friend's dismissiveness
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution mildly humbles both friends rather than being a clean win for the skeptic
assistant_behavior: Sigma names specific credibility markers rather than a blanket dismissal
Sigma does not simply validate whichever friend was more skeptical by default
